Why do dung beetles bury dung balls?

Clouds form when water vapor in the air cools and turns into tiny water droplets. These droplets gather around tiny dust particles in the sky. Millions of droplets together form a cloud. When droplets get heavy enough, they fall to Earth as rain or snow.

What causes water droplets to fall as rain or snow?

steps: Find the condition that causes droplets to fall.
Read: 'When droplets get heavy enough, they fall to Earth as rain or snow.'
The cause is the droplets becoming heavy enough.
solution.answer: When water droplets become heavy enough, they fall to Earth as rain or snow.

Marsupials are a group of animals that carry their newborn young in a pouch. Kangaroos, koalas, and opossums are all marsupials. A newborn marsupial is very tiny and not fully developed. It crawls into its mother's pouch right after birth, where it continues to grow.

Why does a newborn marsupial crawl into its mother's pouch?

steps: Find the reason the newborn goes into the pouch.
Read: 'It crawls into its mother's pouch right after birth, where it continues to grow.'
The reason is to continue growing since it is not fully developed.
solution.answer: A newborn marsupial crawls into its mother's pouch to continue growing, since it is not fully developed at birth.

Rainforests produce about 20 percent of the world's oxygen. They are home to more than half of all plant and animal species. Yet every year, large areas of rainforest are cut down for farming and building. When trees are cut, animals lose their homes and the oxygen those trees produced is lost. Scientists warn that protecting rainforests is critical for life on Earth.

Using two details from the article, explain why scientists think protecting rainforests is critical.

steps: Find two reasons why rainforests are important.
Detail 1: 'Rainforests produce about 20 percent of the world's oxygen.'
Detail 2: 'They are home to more than half of all plant and animal species.'
Both show that rainforests are essential for oxygen and biodiversity.
solution.answer: Rainforests are critical because they produce about 20 percent of the world's oxygen and are home to more than half of all plant and animal species on Earth.

The Dust Bowl was a time in the 1930s when great dust storms swept across the plains of the United States. Farmers had plowed up the native grasses that held the soil in place. When a long drought came, the dry soil had nothing to hold it down. Strong winds picked up the loose soil and created massive dust storms. Thousands of families had to leave their homes and farms.

According to the article, what two things caused the Dust Bowl?

steps: Find the two causes of the Dust Bowl.
Cause 1: Farmers plowed up the native grasses that held the soil in place.
Cause 2: A long drought came, drying out the soil.
Together, these two causes created the conditions for massive dust storms.
solution.answer: The Dust Bowl was caused by farmers plowing up the native grasses that held the soil in place and by a long drought that dried out the unprotected soil.
